identity.name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
native_names: Cộng hòa xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam

land.text: 'North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam' on 2 July 1976: the DRV, which already held the South since 30 April 1975 (see its dossier)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Socialist Republic row begins on 1 January 1976, six months before the merger; both are 1976.

land.text: South Vietnam, the southern half of the merger

predecessors.note: The Vietnam page dates 'End of Vietnam War: 30 April 1975' (infobox) but does not describe the South's government or the interval before the merger; the democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossier records the land passing to the DRV and the provisional revolutionary government in 1975.

capitals.name: Hanoi
capitals.note: Infobox capital Hanoi (21°2′N 105°51′E); the page gives no date for the city becoming capital, and no other seat is named.

keyframe_review.note: 337,618 km2 against the infobox's 331,344.82 km2 (ratio 1.02; the body also gives 331,210 and 331,699). Measured against {country: Vietnam} on the grid the shape has 28 cells outside the modern country and misses 42 of its 1,158, i.e. a coarse coastline and frontier, not a different land. The shape does not move for 1976-2023, which agrees with the pages: the only ground that changed hands was held for weeks (China, Feb-Mar 1979) or tiny (the 1999 border pact). The shape starts in January 1976, six months before the 2 July 1976 merger (same year).
Identical outline to the 1976 shape (Cliopatria repeats it for 2024); nothing on the page changes the land after 1999.

region.text: 'North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam'

ledger.note: 1976: North and South Vietnam are united as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (2 July). Infobox 'Reunification: 2 July 1976'; 'On 2 July 1976, North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.' The page names no capital date and no provisional government.

region.text: the Vietnam-Kampuchea frontier: Dong Thap and Tay Ninh on the Vietnamese side, Svay Rieng Province on the Cambodian side

ledger.note: 1977: Khmer Rouge troops take Vietnamese border ground. In September 1977 'KRA artillery struck several border villages, and six villages in Dong Thap were overrun', then the KRA advanced into Tay Ninh Province (earlier, on 30 April 1977, an attack on An Giang and Chau Doc); from 16 December 1977 the PAVN crossed 'along several axes' and marched through Svay Rieng Province. The page gives no depths, so the zone is the frontier band (confidence 2).

region.text: the Vietnam-Kampuchea frontier and Svay Rieng

ledger.note: December 1978: the frontier fighting gives way to the invasion. 'The Vietnamese military withdrew in January 1978' (the divisions had reached 38 km from Phnom Penh by 6 January), but 'Small-scale fighting continued between the two countries throughout 1978': in January the KRA 'began overrunning Vietnamese outposts in Hà Tiên Province', in April it 'massacred over 3,000 Vietnamese civilians in the village of Ba Chúc', and in June Vietnam 'started bombing KRA positions along the border regions'. The border contest therefore runs until the full-scale invasion of 25 December 1978 (next event); month moved from 1 to 12 by the se-04-c reviewer.

region.text: Democratic Kampuchea, which the page says was occupied in two weeks

ledger.note: 25 December 1978: Vietnam invades Cambodia. 'On 25 December 1978, Vietnam launched a full-scale invasion using 13 divisions, estimated at 150,000 soldiers'; the Kratie offensive had begun on 21 December. Infobox date '23 December 1978 - 26 September 1989'.

7 January 1979: Phnom Penh falls. 'On 7 January 1979, the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS'; the Khmer Rouge 'was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand'. Infobox result: 'Vietnam's overthrow of Democratic Kampuchea in early 1979'.

region.text: Cambodia, whose 'major population centres' the Vietnamese army controlled

ledger.note: 1979: ten years of Vietnamese occupation begin. 'On 8 January 1979 the pro-Vietnamese People's Republic of Kampuchea (PRK) was established in Phnom Penh', 'marking the beginning of a ten-year Vietnamese occupation'; the PRK page says Vietnam's army controlled 'the major population centres' from 1979 to September 1989. The page gives no map, so the whole PRK outline is hatched while the Thai-border strip is carried by the PRK dossier's contest with the Khmer Rouge.

region.text: the border provinces Cao Bang, Lao Cai and Lang Son (and Mong Cai), a strip 15-20 km deep

ledger.note: 17 February 1979: China invades northern Vietnam. 'On 17 February 1979, a People's Liberation Army (PLA) force of about 200,000 troops' crossed; fighting was 'mainly' in Cao Bang, Lao Cai and Lang Son provinces, the PLA advancing about 15-20 km; 'Lang Son fell on 6 March'; Mong Cai was also captured.

region.text: the border strip the PLA had entered

ledger.note: 16 March 1979: the Chinese leave. 'On 6 March, China declared that the gate to Hanoi was open and that their punitive mission had been achieved' and 'The PLA crossed the border back into China on 16 March'; infobox result 'Status quo ante bellum, both sides claim victory'. 'Border skirmishes continued throughout the 1980s', with a significant one in April 1984; the page gives no ground held.

September 1989: Vietnam withdraws from Cambodia. 'The remaining 26,000 left between 21 and 26 September 1989' (24,000 had left between April and July); the Sino-Vietnamese War page: 'Armed conflict only ended in 1989 after the Vietnamese agreed to fully withdraw from Cambodia.' The PRK page notes the last troops 'probably did not leave until 1990'.

region.text: part of Vietnam's land around the Friendship Pass (Ai Nam Quan) on the Chinese frontier

ledger.note: 1999: the land border pact with China. 'In 1999, after many years of negotiations, China and Vietnam signed a border pact', which the page glosses as 'Vietnam giving China part of its land which was lost during the battle', naming the Ai Nam Quan (Friendship Pass) gate among the areas affected. The page gives neither the day nor the area; the region is the Vietnamese frontier strip within 30 km of Lang Son, the nearest listed place (confidence 2; the area really moved is far smaller than the 3 cells drawn).

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War

zones.text: the December 1978 invasion of Democratic Kampuchea

wars.outcome: Vietnam overthrows Democratic Kampuchea in early 1979 and installs the People's Republic of Kampuchea; its army occupies Cambodia until September 1989; the 1991 Paris Peace Accords follow.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war 23 December 1978 - 26 September 1989; the page's text begins the fighting with the Khmer Rouge raids of 1977. The K5 Plan was unveiled in 1984 and its first phase completed in the 1984-85 dry-season offensive; the page gives no map of control.

wars.name: Sino-Vietnamese War
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum, both sides claim victory (infobox): the PLA withdrew on 16 March 1979; a 1999 border pact later moved a small area to China.
wars.note: Skirmishes continued through the 1980s (April 1984; the Johnson South Reef naval clash of 1988 in the Spratlys); normalisation 'in November 1991'. The page names no ground held after March 1979.

certainty.note: A modern state with administrative frontiers. The Chinese frontier was disputed until the 1999 pact ('after many years of negotiations'); the Cambodian frontier was fought over in 1977-78; the Vietnam page gives 4,639 km of land boundary but no treaty dates and the sea claims are not territory here.

notes: Written for batch se-04-c with three pages (Vietnam, Cambodian-Vietnamese War, Sino-Vietnamese War); the budget was 1-2, exceeded by one because the two wars are the only things that move this state's border. Cliopatria: both shapes are the same outline (337,618 km2, ratio 1.02 to the infobox); the row starts in January 1976, the merger is 2 July 1976. The state is the successor of the democratic-republic-of-vietnam (its dossier dissolves into this one) and of the republic-of-vietnam (South Vietnam, dossier of another part of se-04). Page silent: Vietnamese troops in Laos and the 1977 Vietnam-Laos treaty (the Cambodian-Vietnamese War page only has three divisions based in Laos in 1978 and 1,000 Lao soldiers in 1988); the 1985 Vietnam-Cambodia border treaty; the exact day of the 1999 Sino-Vietnamese pact and the 2000 Gulf of Tonkin agreement; the Paracel and Spratly disputes (the Vietnam page does not name them); the Chinese-held hills of the 1980s (Vi Xuyen, Laoshan, Lao Cai), which the Sino-Vietnamese War page does not describe, so no 1980s occupation is recorded. Counterparts: people-s-republic-of-china (ea-08) should carry the matching contest of Feb-Mar 1979 and a gain in 1999; khmer-rouge (another se-04 part) the matching 1977-79 contests; people-s-republic-of-kampuchea (this batch) the matching occupation. The People's Republic of Kampuchea is hatched as a Vietnamese occupation (the page's word) rather than drawn as a vassal tint. The 1999 loss uses the frontier band within 30 km of Lang Son (3 cells) because the page names only the Friendship Pass and the gazetteer has no pass entry (Friendship Pass / Huu Nghi / Ai Nam Quan / Dong Dang); the area actually moved is far below one cell. No rulers are given (no list was opened).
